addedLines: - agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-py: Use this agent to verify that a Python Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a Python Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts: Use this agent to verify that a TypeScript Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>
Context: User wants to create a code review agent
user: "Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate the agent configuration."
<commentary>
User requesting new agent creation, trigger agent-creator to generate it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User describes needed functionality
user: "I need an agent that generates unit tests for my code"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to create a test generation agent."
<commentary>
User describes agent need, trigger agent-creator to build it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User wants to add agent to plugin
user: "Add an agent to my plugin that validates configurations"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate a configuration validator agent."
<commentary>
Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

- plugin-dev:plugin-validator: Use this agent when the user asks to "validate my plugin", "check plugin structure", "verify plugin is correct", "validate plugin.json", "check plugin files", or mentions plugin validation. Also trigger proactively after user creates or modifies plugin components. Examples:

<example>
Context: User finished creating a new plugin
user: "I've created my first plugin with commands and hooks"
assistant: "Great! Let me validate the plugin structure."
<commentary>
Plugin created, proactively validate to catch issues early.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the plugin."
</example>

<example>
Context: User explicitly requests validation
user: "Validate my plugin before I publish it"
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to perform comprehensive validation."
<commentary>
Explicit validation request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified plugin.json
user: "I've updated the plugin manifest"
assistant: "Let me validate the changes."
<commentary>
Manifest modified, validate to ensure correctness.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the manifest."
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

<example>
Context: User just created a new skill
user: "I've created a PDF processing skill"
assistant: "Great! Let me review the skill quality."
<commentary>
Skill created, proactively trigger skill-reviewer to ensure it follows best practices.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the skill."
</example>

<example>
Context: User requests skill review
user: "Review my skill and tell me how to improve it"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to analyze the skill quality."
<commentary>
Explicit skill review request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified skill description
user: "I updated the skill description, does it look good?"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the changes."
<commentary>
Skill description modified, review for triggering effectiveness.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

## ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
- upstream-sync-review: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
- agent-sdk-dev:new-sdk-app: Create and setup a new Claude Agent SDK application
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- commit-commands:clean_gone: Cleans up all git branches marked as [gone] (branches that have been deleted on the remote but still exist locally), including removing associated worktrees.
- commit-commands:commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR
- commit-commands:commit: Create a git commit
- feature-dev:feature-dev: Guided feature development with codebase understanding and architecture focus
- plugin-dev:create-plugin: Guided end-to-end plugin creation workflow with component design, implementation, and validation
- pr-review-toolkit:review-pr: Comprehensive PR review using specialized agents
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- vercel:bootstrap: Bootstrap a repository with Vercel-linked resources by running preflight checks, provisioning integrations, verifying env keys, and then executing db/dev startup commands safely.
- vercel:deploy: Deploy the current project to Vercel. Pass "prod" or "production" as argument to deploy to production. Default is preview deployment.
- vercel:env: Manage Vercel environment variables. Commands include list, pull, add, remove, and diff. Use to sync environment variables between Vercel and your local development environment.
- vercel:status: Show the status of the current Vercel project — recent deployments, linked project info, and environment overview.
- claude-code-setup:claude-automation-recommender: Analyze a codebase and recommend Claude Code automations (hooks, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers). Use when user asks for automation recommendations, wants to optimize their Claude Code setup, mentions improving Claude Code workflows, asks how to first set up Claude Code for a project, or wants to know what Claude Code features they should use.
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/session-start

Run the mandatory session start ritual defined in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do this before writing any code.

## Steps (in order — do not skip any)

1. **Confirm branch** — run `git branch --show-current`. If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — no edits permitted (see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 1). If it matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`, read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) in full before proceeding — the supervised-edit and back-merge rules there apply on top of the Hard Rules.

2. **Read tracking docs** — read these in parallel:
   - [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md) — current phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending
   - [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](../../../.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) — what exists this sprint, what is deferred. **Read before scoping any new work.**
   - [.docs/memory/feedback.md](../../../.docs/memory/feedback.md) — patterns to avoid or repeat
   - [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) — current `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version and review state
   - [../session-notes.md](../session-notes.md) — lightweight, **gitignored, per-developer** carryover notes from your last local session (a Claude-writable staging area — see "Living Memory" below for how this differs from `.docs/memory/`). If it has pending items, surface them in step 4's "blockers or outstanding issues" and clear/promote each once resolved. It won't exist for a fresh clone or a teammate who hasn't used it — that's expected, skip silently.

3. **Health checks** — run when the helper exists:
   - `bash scripts/healthCheckAll.sh` — If the script does not exist yet, state that clearly and skip.

4. **State current position** — in plain language, say exactly:
   - Current branch
   - Current sprint / phase (from `projectState.md`)
   - The last completed task and the next task
   - Any blockers or outstanding issues

   Format: "Resuming from: [last completed task]. Next: [next task]. [Any blockers or health issues]."

5. **Confirm readiness** — ask if the user wants to proceed with the stated next task or redirect to something else.

Do not write any code until this ritual is complete and the user has confirmed direction.

---

## Living Memory — what belongs where

`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Keep it current — update the relevant file whenever a session produces new information that belongs there.

**`.claude/session-notes.md` is different: a lightweight, Claude-writable, gitignored, per-developer staging area** (same pattern as `userProfile.md` below, but for tasks rather than profile info) for short-lived carryover items (e.g. "still need to do X next session") that haven't been promoted to `.docs/memory/` yet. It's **not** shared via git — each developer's notes stay local, so they never conflict or overwrite a teammate's. Unlike the files below, Claude may write to it directly. Use it for quick pending-item tracking; move anything durable and team-relevant into the right `.docs/memory/` file once it's confirmed, and clear the note.

| File | What belongs there | When to update |
|---|---|---|
| `architecture.md` | Stack decisions, overrides pattern, key paths, structural choices | A new integration is added, a structural decision is made, or a key path changes |
| `projectState.md` | Phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending, unresolved dependencies | Any integration goes live, a phase changes, a feature is completed, or a dependency is resolved |
| `feedback.md` | What worked, what failed, patterns to avoid or repeat | After discovering a gotcha, a failed approach, or a validated pattern |
| `references.md` | Service URLs, API keys, credentials, logins, dashboards | A new credential or service URL is introduced (system roles live in `architecture.md`) |
| `userProfile.md` | User's role, expertise, working style, preferences | User shares a preference or working-style detail that should persist |

**Rules:**
- Never leave a file with only its placeholder comment — populate it the moment you learn something that belongs there.
- **No duplication.** Every fact has exactly one home. Before writing something, check whether it already lives in another doc — if it does, reference that doc instead of copying. Applies across all `.md` files: `AGENTS.md`, memory files, and PRDs.
- **Conciseness.** Keep all `.md` instructions concise.
I'll run the session-start ritual now.

This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com).   (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.

===== DESCRIPTION =====
**As a** Shopper,

**I want** to see all available colours for a product and be able to switch between them on the page,

**so that** I can explore the full range of colour options before choosing which to buy.

----

Image for reference (final design in Figma is leading):

!["image-20260701-114754.png"](image-20260701-114754.png)

This story covers the rendering of colour swatches on the PDP and the interaction logic when a shopper selects a different colour. Swatches are driven by the index image — one product image per colour variation that is designated in SFCC BM as the representative swatch image.

Most products do not have a wide range of colours available, however, Dani confirmed max needed number of colours will likely be around **7.** 

Here’s a current product that has 4 colours:[Lumi Sandal Lilac Online ]( Zimmermann|https://www.zimmermann.com/shoes/flats-sneakers/lumi-sandal-lilac.html)

########## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA CHANGE HISTORY ##########
*Swatch availability*

* Given a product has only one colour, when the PDP loads, then the colour is displayed as a text label (e.g. "Colour: Bay Blue") and no swatches are rendered.
* Given a product has multiple colour variations, when the PDP loads, then the index image for each colour variation is displayed as a swatch.
* Given multiple colour swatches are displayed, when the PDP loads, then the currently viewed colour variation's swatch is visually indicated as selected.

*Swatch selection*

* Colour variation: Given a shopper clicks a colour swatch, when the selection is registered, then the URL updates to reflect the selected colour variation without full page reload. 
* New Style Code: Given a shopper clicks a colour swatch, when the selection is registered, then the URL updates to reflect the selected colour with a new style code and a full page reload.

*Index image not populated*

* Given a colour variation exists but has no index image designated, when the PDP loads, then that colour variation's swatch is not rendered and the variation is not surfaced to the shopper (pending confirmation of fallback behaviour — see dependencies).

input.content: # SFCC-91 — PDP UI: Colour Swatches & Variation Selection > **Temporary working notes.** Scratch file for the PR #70 review session. > Not part of the repo. Source of truth remains Jira + Figma. > Pulled from Jira: **2026-08-28** **Jira:** https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-91 **PR under review:** https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/70 **Branch:** `feature/SFCC-91_pdp-ui-colour-swatches-variation-selection` → `develop` --- ## 1. Ticket at a glance | Field | Value | |---|---| | **Type** | Story | | **Status** | **Code Review** (moved 2026-08-28 by Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz) | | **Priority** | High | | **Story points** | 3 | | **Sprint** | **SFCC Sprint 4** (25 Aug – 7 Sep 2026) — carried over from Sprint 3 | | **Due date** | 2026-08-27 *(already passed)* | | **Assignee** | Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz | | **Reporter** | Jasmijn Tsang | | **Epic (parent)** | [SFCC-5 — Product Detail Page (PDP)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-5) *(In Progress)* | | **Labels** | `Custom`, `DesignDependent`, `PRD-002`, `PRD-004`, `Squad-A` | | **Created** | 2026-07-01 | | **Last updated** | 2026-08-28 | **Rollout scope — all 8 storefronts:** AU · ME · EU-Domestic · EU-International · HK · UK · US-Domestic · US-International > ⚠️ Squad label was changed from **Squad-B → Squad-A** on 2026-07-09. --- ## 2. User story (verbatim) > **As a** Shopper, > > **I want** to see all available colours for a product and be able to switch between them on the page, > > **so that** I can explore the full range of colour options before choosing which to buy. ### Description notes - Covers **rendering of colour swatches on the PDP** and the **interaction logic** when a shopper selects a different colour. - **Swatches are driven by the index image** — one product image per colour variation, designated in SFCC BM as the representative swatch image. - Most products do not have a wide colour range. **Dani confirmed max ≈ 7 colours.** - Real-world reference product (4 colours): Lumi Sandal Lilac. - Reference image is attached to the ticket, **but "final design in Figma is leading"**. --- ## 3. Acceptance Criteria (CURRENT — verbatim from Jira) ### Swatch availability 1. Given a product has **only one colour**, when the PDP loads, then the colour is displayed as a **text label** (e.g. "Colour: Bay Blue") and **no swatches are rendered**. 2. Given a product has **multiple colour variations**, when the PDP loads, then **the index image for each colour variation is displayed as a swatch**. 3. Given multiple colour swatches are displayed, when the PDP loads, then the **currently viewed colour variation's swatch is visually indicated as selected**. ### Swatch selection 4. **Colour variation:** Given a shopper clicks a colour swatch, when the selection is registered, then the **URL updates** to reflect the selected colour variation **without full page reload**. ### Index image not populated 5. Given a colour variation exists **but has not been enabled**, when the PDP loads, then that colour variation's swatch is **not rendered** and the variation is **not surfaced** to the shopper. --- ## 4. Scope boundaries — what this ticket does NOT cover This is the part that matters most for reviewing PR #70. The AC set was **actively narrowed twice**. ### 4.1 Moved OUT to [SFCC-708](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-708) — *Related Colours Attribute (BM / frontend)* Removed from SFCC-91 on **2026-08-12** by Jasmijn Tsang, who wrote: > "I removed this ac from this ticket: *New Style Code: Given a shopper clicks a colour swatch, when the selection is registered, then the URL updates to reflect the selected colour with a new style code and a full page reload.* This requires more build - we will cover this AC in SFCC-708" And earlier the same day: > "This cannot yet be tested… We need a product attribute for this in BM. I'll create a story for that now." **SFCC-708 (status: Ready for Development) owns:** - The `Related Colours` attribute in Business Manager (comma-separated style codes, as per Magento). - Linking **separate master products** that are *not* natural colour variants of the same master. - Swatch **display order** driven by the order of style codes in that field. - **Full page reload** navigation to a new style code. - Invalid related product ID → swatch does not render. - Valid ID but product **not online** (offline flag / outside online date range) → swatch does not render. > **Review implication:** PR #70 should handle **intra-master colour variations only**. Cross-master "related colours", style-code URL changes, and full-page-reload navigation are **out of scope** and should not appear in this PR. ### 4.2 Silently dropped AC — ⚠️ FLAG An AC present at ticket creation (2026-07-01) was **removed on 2026-07-02** and never reinstated: > ~~"Given a shopper navigates directly to a colour variation URL, when the page loads, then the correct colour variation PDP is displayed and its swatch is shown as selected."~~ It was replaced by the "New Style Code" AC — which itself was later moved to SFCC-708. **Net effect: the deep-link / direct-URL-entry behaviour is currently specified nowhere.** AC #3 ("currently viewed colour variation's swatch is visually indicated as selected") arguably implies it on load, but the explicit deep-link case is gone. **→ Worth raising with Jasmijn: is direct-URL colour entry covered by SFCC-91, SFCC-708, or neither?** ### 4.3 Out of scope per the sibling story [SFCC-89](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-89) (Static Product Information) SFCC-89 explicitly lists "Colour swatches and variation selection" as out of *its* scope — confirming the split. Conversely, **not** SFCC-91's job: product name, price, description, "Model is…" copy, style code, breadcrumbs. ### 4.4 Also not this ticket - **Size selector / availability states** — separate story. - **Image gallery** behaviour — separate story (though colour switch presumably updates it). - **Badges, Was/Now price** ([SFCC-194](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-194), PR #68), **Wishlist/CTAs**, **accordion content**, **Contentful content**. --- ## 5. Dependencies **Current (Jira `Dependency` field):** - ✅ *"This story has a hard dependency on the index image attribute being defined."* **Historical dependencies since resolved/removed:** - ~~Max number of colours + behaviour when a colour is unavailable~~ → answered 2026-07-07: **max ≈ 7** (Dani, via Jasmijn). *Note: the "does an unavailable colour show at swatch level?" half of that question does not have a recorded answer.* - ~~Separate user story for URL / SEO / GEO / paid-marketing discussion with Mani~~ → became SFCC-708. - ~~Final Figma design pending sign-off~~ → removed 2026-07-03 when the Figma link was added. **Blocking links (both now Done):** - `is blocked by` [SFCC-205](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-205) — Spike: Figma to React Setup ✅ Done - `is blocked by` [SFCC-240](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-240) — Spike: Figma-to-React Implementation Workflow ✅ Done **Related links:** - `relates to` [SFCC-708](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-708) — Related Colours Attribute *(Ready for Development)* - `relates to` [SFCC-737](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-737) — `pdp/product-content` *(In Progress, same assignee)* - `relates to` [SFCC-806](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-806) — Development task, Sprint 3 ✅ Done --- ## 6. Design / Technical Notes (verbatim from Jira) > **Link to Figma design:** https://www.figma.com/design/QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs/Zimmermann_Final-Approved-Designs?node-id=3087-15747 > > - The URL should update when a different colour or size is selected - without a full page reload ### Reference image (attached to ticket, `image-20260701-114754.png`) Shows: - A **"Color: Raspberry"** text label above the swatch row. - Swatches rendered as **full product index images** (not colour chips/dots) — two dresses shown side by side. - Selected state indicated by a **solid underline bar** beneath the selected swatch. > ⚠️ **Spelling:** the mock reads "Color:" (US). Project convention is **Australian spelling** (`.claude/rules/conventions.md`), and AC #1 uses "Colour: Bay Blue". Copy should be **"Colour"**, and in any case must be **i18n'd**, not hardcoded — this is an 8-storefront, 11-locale rollout. --- ## 7. Composition context — SFCC-737 `pdp/product-content` SFCC-91's swatch component is consumed by the `pdp/product-content` panel: > "The component is a composition container. **It does not own the logic of its child components** — interaction behaviour for colour selection, size selection, add to bag, wishlist, and drawer triggers are covered in their respective child component stories." **→ Separation of concerns is explicit:** colour-selection *interaction logic* belongs to SFCC-91's component; `pdp/product-content` only handles layout/ordering. This aligns with the repo rule in `.claude/rules/components.md` — **container/presentational separation**: components under `overrides/app/components/` receive data as props and must not call data-fetching hooks themselves. --- ## 8. Timeline / history (condensed) | Date | Event | |---|---| | 2026-07-01 | Created by Jasmijn Tsang. Initial ACs include **direct-URL deep link** AC. | | 2026-07-02 | PO approved. PR #70 raised. | --- ## 9. Open questions / risks to carry into the PR review 1. **⚠️ >4-colour design gap.** Hazel flagged on 2026-08-26: *"Pending on the design for more than 4-colour variant."* Dani said max ≈ 7, and the Figma reference only shows 2. **How does the swatch row behave at 5, 6, 7 colours — wrap, scroll, truncate?** No recorded answer. ### The 5 current ACs

2. Multiple colours → index image per variation rendered as a swatch
3. Currently-viewed variation's swatch is **visually selected**
4. Click a swatch → **URL updates, no full page reload**
5. Variation not enabled → swatch **not rendered**, variation not surfaced

## The part that matters for reviewing PR #70

The AC set was **deliberately narrowed**, and one AC went missing in the shuffle.

**Moved out to [SFCC-708](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-708)** on 12 Aug — Jasmijn: *"This requires more build - we will cover this AC in SFCC-708"*. That story owns the BM `Related Colours` attribute, cross-master style-code linking, **full page reload**, swatch ordering, and invalid/offline product handling. **⚠️ An AC was silently dropped and never reinstated.** The original 1 Jul ticket had:

> ~~"Given a shopper navigates directly to a colour variation URL, when the page loads, then the correct colour variation PDP is displayed and its swatch is shown as selected."~~

It was overwritten on 2 Jul by the "New Style Code" AC — which then moved to SFCC-708 on 12 Aug. **Deep-link / direct-URL colour entry is now specified in neither ticket.** Given AC #4 mandates URL updates, having no AC for *arriving* at that URL is a real gap.

- **"Colour unavailable at swatch level"** — Jasmijn asked this on 7 Jul, only the max-colours half got answered. AC #5 covers *not enabled*, not *out of stock*.
- **Index image attribute** is the one remaining hard dependency — if it isn't populated in the sandbox, ACs #2 and #5 aren't testable.
- **Design mock says "Color:"** (US). Convention is Australian spelling, and it must be i18n'd regardless — 11 locales.
- Swatches being *product images* collides directly with the perf rule about not rendering full-res images at thumbnail size.

One thing I'd flag as a judgment call: the ticket is in **Code Review with an unresolved design dependency** (the >4-colour case). Worth deciding whether that blocks approval or gets split out, before we start reading the diff.

content.text:
I've got a complete picture. Here's the review.

## PR #70 — SFCC-91 Colour Swatches

**Verdict: solid feature work, but three unrelated changes are riding along, and one "fix" made things worse.** CodeRabbit approved at 04:57, and the author replied in-thread to every finding (correct per AGENTS.md). The issues below are ones CodeRabbit either missed or caused.

### What's genuinely good

Container/presentational split is clean — pure props, no SDK hooks. a11y is properly done (real radiogroup/radio, roving `tabIndex`, `aria-checked`, decorative `alt=""` with the name on the button). Perf is handled — `sw=96&q=60` DIS sizing directly addresses the "never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size" rule, which matters a lot when swatches *are* product photos. 19 Vitest tests plus 5 Storybook `play` functions, and pagination is properly covered at the play layer. New strings are i18n'd with Australian spelling.

---

### 1. 🔴 Out-of-scope visual change to cart, wishlist and bonus-product

[`product-view/index.tsx:838`](overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:838)

```diff
- variant={id === 'color' ? 'circle' : 'square'}
+ variant="square"
```

Both variants exist in the base theme and are **substantially different** — `circle` is an 11×11 round swatch with `borderRadius: 'full'`; `square` is a bordered, padded box with a diagonal-line disabled state. We don't override swatch-group, so base styles apply.

The PDP doesn't need this — it suppresses colour entirely via `suppressColourAttribute`. So the only surfaces affected are **cart quick-add, wishlist, and bonus-product**, which get their colour swatches silently restyled from round to square. That's a design change with no UI-designer sign-off, it's undisclosed in the PR body, and it contradicts the PR's own test-plan line claiming non-PDP consumers are unaffected.

### 2. 🔴 `filterImageGroups` was duplicated to satisfy a false-positive, and the justification is factually wrong

[`overrides/app/utils/filterImageGroups.ts`](overrides/app/utils/filterImageGroups.ts) — 43 lines reimplementing upstream. Its header comment says:

> *"that path is an internal module with no public export"*

That's not true. It's `export const filterImageGroups` at `product-utils.js:182`, and [`product-detail/index.tsx:26`](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:26) imports `getUpdateBundleChildArray` **from that exact module specifier**, two lines above the new import. The stability-boundary argument is applied to one function and not its neighbour.

CodeRabbit raised this as Major based on a web query about "supported public package entrypoints" — but `conventions.md` bans `node_modules/@salesforce/...` *filesystem* paths, not `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` specifiers, which is what the code already used and what this repo uses throughout.

Worse: **the copy has no test.** `conventions.md` requires Vitest for any utility with ≥1 conditional branch — this has several. The upstream original *is* tested (`product-utils.test.js:692`). So the change traded tested code for untested duplicated code.

### 3. 🟠 Quantity label change — out of scope, and reduces localisability

[`product-view/index.tsx:870`](overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:870) moves the colon out of the message and hardcodes it in JSX. On `develop`, all 26 locale files already store `Quantity`/`Antal`/`Quantité` without a colon, so this is a **visible change in every locale**, not a no-op.

It also removes the ability to localise the punctuation — French wants `Quantité :` with a narrow no-break space, Japanese and Chinese want full-width `：`. Nothing to do with SFCC-91.

### 4. 🟠 Undisclosed Tier 2 change

`protectedFiles.md` lists **`translations/` and `overrides/app/static/translations/` as Tier 2** (Integration / SI Partner — notify before changing). Nine translation files changed. The PR body's tier table lists only `theme/components/index.ts` as Tier 2 — and omits 12 of 27 changed files entirely, including `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` (+61 lines of build tooling) and the new util.

Also worth stating explicitly: only 4 of 26 locales got the new `colour_swatches.*` keys. The other 22 fall back to English `defaultMessage` — fine pre-translation, but it should be said out loud on an 8-storefront rollout.

### 5. 🟡 Styling layer inconsistency

[`colourSwatches/index.tsx:185`](overrides/app/components/product-view/colourSwatches/index.tsx:185) sets `sx={{ marginTop: 'var(--zimm-scale-1100)' }}` in JSX, while `marginBottom` for the *same element* lives in the recipe's `container` slot. Tokens belong in the recipe — this is the split that PR #56 deleted.

### 6. 🟡 Parent doesn't memoise `colourVariants`

[`product-detail/index.tsx:283`](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:283) is an IIFE that re-runs `filterImageGroups` per colour on every render and returns a **new array identity every time**. That's precisely what forced the component's `swatchVariantsRef` + `swatchVariantsKey` + `eslint-disable` machinery. A `useMemo` in the parent lets most of that be deleted.

### 7. 🟡 AC5: `orderable: false` is being treated as "not enabled"

AC5 says *"has not been enabled"*. The code hides **out-of-stock** colours entirely. The code comment claims *"confirmed by the BA 2026-08-21"* — but the Jira question from 2026-07-07 (*"check when other colour is unavailable, does it show on the swatch level"*) is **still unanswered in the ticket**. That decision currently exists only in a code comment.

Edge case: if *every* colour is non-orderable, `hasOfferedColour` is false → `suppressColourAttribute` is false → the base SwatchGroup renders instead, now square. Inconsistent PDP depending on stock state.

---

I have not run `tsc`/tests myself — those claims are the PR's. I can verify in a throwaway worktree so your branch state and stashes stay untouched. Want me to do that, and/or draft the in-thread PR replies for these?

3	Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.

attachment.content:
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. # Styling an Override Component

How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
companion.

---

## The hierarchy — reach for these in order

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
   type" below.
4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.

**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
which is what `audit:tokens` is for.

## Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
  comment for traceability.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy

`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
if only one of them is ever typed.

`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.

## One canonical styling surface per component type

Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
there's no interactive state to lose.

## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component

If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import, which is correct for that file).

The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
override and isn't.

**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.

An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.

## Component-local tokens

When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
— `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
`marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.

See `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` and
`.../footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` for the pattern in a real recipe. The reason is
traceability, not parity with the base theme: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference names the
Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these

Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these
recipes are deliberately namespaced `ZimmFooter*` so they do **not** inherit the base
SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)

**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

The array shorthand (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`) is what this section used to
recommend, and it would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks
responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail.
`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.

When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
`header.ts`/`zimmButton.css.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.

## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)

If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put
Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default and adds
brand-specific defaults, the same split `product-tile/index.tsx` (`CardBaseline`
name + default) and `link/index.tsx` already use. `image-gallery`, `display-price`, and
`swatch-group` are all shared internal SFCC dependencies. When one of them does get
overridden, keep its default export API-compatible and put brand styling in a theme
recipe rather than a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't require a second
export the way `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.

**As of `7b9b5dc`, none of the three is overridden at all** — no component override, no
theme recipe, nothing registered for them in `theme/components/index.ts`. Verify current
state before relying on any of this. `protectedFiles.md` and `CODEOWNERS` list those
paths forward-lookingly, not descriptively. An earlier revision of this paragraph cited
`theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` as holding their styling; neither
file has ever existed on any branch.

---

## Co-locating a component's theme file

A component's recipe may live beside it as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g.
`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, or an organism's own
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/<name>/<name>.css.ts`) instead of in
`theme/components/`. Either way it's still registered in
`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key
passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path, so co-location is purely an
organisational choice with no runtime difference.

**Governance follows the file, not the folder.** `theme/components/` is Tier 2, gated to
the UI designer (protectedFiles.md). A co-located `<name>.css.ts` is deliberately routed
differently: CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule sends it to the
owning squad(s) only, dropping the Tier 1/2 approver requirement that the surrounding
directory (e.g. `header/`, `footer/`) otherwise carries. That's intentional — a co-located
file is for composing a component's own layout from **already-established** tokens
(spacing, colour, typography scale), not for authoring new raw design values. Authoring an
actual new token still means editing `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a `theme/components/`
recipe that's still designer-owned (`header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts` — the
files that remain in that directory) — both stay behind the full gate.

> **Known inconsistency, flagged not resolved.** This paragraph used to cite `button.ts`'s
> `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y` as the designer-gated example. That file
> is now `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`, which the `**/*.css.ts` rule above
> routes to the squads — so those provisional, unapproved constants are **no longer
> designer-gated**, while still keying the app-wide `Button` recipe. The example was swapped
> to `header.ts` (genuinely still gated) so this paragraph stops asserting something false.
> Whether `zimmButton.css.ts` should be re-gated is an open governance question, not a doc
> fix, and is deliberately left open here.

**Enforcement gap, partially closed:** the Tier 1/2 human reviewer was, until this rule
existed, the only thing catching a hardcoded hex/px/rem/em value landing in a theme file.
`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (`npm run audit:tokens`, see the `Never` note above) now exists
and runs correctly against the real codebase — built 2026-08-23. What's still open: it is not
wired into CI, so it only catches something if a developer or reviewer remembers to run it —
removing the Tier 1/2 reviewer from co-located `.css.ts` files still removes an *automatic*
backstop for exactly the files most likely to need it. Wiring `audit:tokens` as a required CI
check on `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` is the remaining near-term follow-up, not an
optional nice-to-have — and per the script's own header, someone should triage a full run's
findings first (14 pre-existing, unrelated violations turned up the day it was built) before
turning it into a hard gate.

**Cross-file shared values** (a breakpoint or provisional size needed by more than one
split-out file) go in a small shared module that stays in `theme/components/` — e.g.
`footerShared.ts`, holding the breakpoints and the one size value `footerNavColumn.css.ts`
and `bottomBar.css.ts` both need. Don't copy the same literal into two co-located files;
that's exactly the drift risk "The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy" (above)
already warns about.

Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these

SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)

**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

The array shorthand (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`) is what this section used to
recommend, and it would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks
responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail.
`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.

When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
`header.ts`/`zimmButton.css.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.

## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)

If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put
Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default and adds
brand-specific defaults, the same split `product-tile/index.tsx` (`CardBaseline`
name + default) and `link/index.tsx` already use. `image-gallery`, `display-price`, and
`swatch-group` are all shared internal SFCC dependencies. When one of them does get
overridden, keep its default export API-compatible and put brand styling in a theme
recipe rather than a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't require a second
export the way `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.

**As of `7b9b5dc`, none of the three is overridden at all** — no component override, no
theme recipe, nothing registered for them in `theme/components/index.ts`. Verify current
state before relying on any of this. `protectedFiles.md` and `CODEOWNERS` list those
paths forward-lookingly, not descriptively. An earlier revision of this paragraph cited
`theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` as holding their styling; neither
file has ever existed on any branch.

A component's recipe may live beside it as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g.
