content.content:
=== the actual scope computation (id: scope) ===
        id: scope
        # ALL/HOMEPAGE go through env: rather than being interpolated
        # directly into the script — a changed_files output is built from
        # real filenames in the diff, and interpolating one straight into
        # `run:` would let a filename containing quotes/shell syntax break
        # out of the assignment and execute on the runner (zizmor:
        # template-injection). Reading from env avoids that entirely.
        env:
          ALL: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_all_changed_files }}
          HOMEPAGE: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_homepage_all_changed_files }}
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ github.base_ref }}" == release/* ]]; then
            echo "e2e_scope=full" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          if [[ -z "$ALL" ]]; then
            echo "e2e_scope=skip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          # also in the homepage allow-list — a single file outside it (a

## Verification results (run by me, on the branch)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | ✅ **PASS** — exit 0, zero output |
| `npm run test` | ✅ **PASS** — 407/407, 27 files, incl. `recipeGuards.test.ts` |

| `npm run audit:tokens` | ⚠️ exit 1, but **all 4 failures are pre-existing** in `header/*`; the PR's own files are properly acknowledged |

**On `audit:tokens` — the PR is in the clear.** The 4 failures are byte-identical on `develop` and none of those files are in this PR. The PR body's claim is substantively right, just imprecise about the exit code.

**On lint — it is not.** The PR body's test plan lists tsc, test, build, audit:tokens but **not lint**, and it shows. All 9 new errors are in this PR's own lines (git-blamed):

- `colourSwatches/index.tsx` — 4 errors, incl. a real one: `Avoid referencing unbound methods` on the `useIntl` destructure. **`staticProductHeader.tsx` already solves exactly this** with a documented `eslint-disable` — the new component didn't follow the established pattern.
- `staticProductHeader.test.tsx` — unnecessary type assertion
- `product-view/index.tsx:80` — the stray blank line the diff adds
- `product-detail/index.tsx:271, 286` — prettier

Also: **both `eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` directives the author added are dead** — ESLint reports "no problems were reported" for each. The elaborate `swatchVariantsRef` + `swatchVariantsKey` machinery those suppressions accompany may be more defensive than it needs to be.

## The one that worries me most

AC4 — *"URL updates without full page reload"*, the single behavioural AC of this story — has **zero executing coverage at every layer**:

1. **No unit test** — nothing in either test file touches `handleColourSelect`, `history.replace`, or `?color=`
2. **All 11 Playwright specs skip** — every one gated on an unprovisioned `E2E_*_SKU`
3. **`e2e-localhost` won't run at all.** `qa.yml` has exactly one area allow-list, `e2e_homepage`. This PR touches none of it, so `SCOPE="skip"` — I read the actual shell logic, not just the docs

The specs are correctly tagged `['@pdp', '@SFCC-91']`, but `pdp` was never registered as an area — so the tag buys nothing here.

Two corrections to my earlier review, both caused by the same thing: **the `.claude/rules/` loaded at session start were the July versions from that stale onboarding branch.** The current rules differ substantially, including a new 280-line `overrideStyling.md`.

- **My "tokens in JSX" finding was wrong.** `overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2 makes `var(--zimm-*)` in JSX the *required* form; bare Chakra keys are the banned thing. I had it backwards.
- **The circle→square finding got stronger.** `overrideStyling.md`'s Known-gaps section explicitly flags swatch-group's `square`/`circle` variants as *"real visual design decisions with no Zimmermann Figma spec behind them yet"* — so silently switching them in a swatches PR touches a knowingly designer-unowned area.

Waiting on the architecture-alignment agent and the CodeRabbit CLI run before I give the verdict — the duplication question (whether a `ProductDetailOptions` colour-swatch implementation already exists) could move it either way.

## 1. DUPLICATION CHECK — CLEAN (the doc is wrong, not the code)

**CERTAIN. No duplicate exists.** `ProductDetailOptions` does **not** exist anywhere under `overrides/` — on this branch, on `develop`, or on any other local/remote ref. Full-repo grep returns exactly three hits, all inside the rule file that mentions it:

- `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:108` — `If component A (e.g. \`productDetailOptions\`) uses component B, and B already has an override (e.g. \`swatch-group\`)…`
- `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:254-257` — `None of those exist as overrides yet, so \`ProductDetailOptions\` ships without them — it's colour/size swatches, quantity, and add-to-bag only.`

That "ships" is **aspirational prose about an f2r prototype, not a description of this repo.** The real artifacts:
- `f2r/02-design/library/elements/product-detail-options/{demo.html, zimm-product-detail-options.css, .js}` — vanilla HTML/CSS/JS design-library files, only on the unmerged `f2r-*` branches. There is no `f2r/` directory on this branch or on `develop`.
- `f2r-implementation-workflow:overrides/app/components/ui-kits/registry.tsx:857` — `{ name: 'zimm-product-detail-options', label: 'ProductDetailOptions', tier: 'molecule', placeholder: true }` — explicitly `placeholder: true`, on an unmerged branch.

Also **CERTAIN**: `overrides/app/components/swatch-group/` does not exist (matches overrideStyling.md's own "As of `7b9b5dc`, none of the three is overridden at all"). A scan of every local and remote ref for `colourSwatch|colorSwatch|swatch-group|productDetailOptions` under `overrides/` returns only this PR's own four files.

**The one real overlap** is intra-PR and is handled deliberately: `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:798-799` skips the colour attribute in the base `SwatchGroup` loop when `suppressColourAttribute` is set, so PDP renders `ColourSwatches` and cart/wishlist/bonus-modal keep base `SwatchGroup`. That's two colour-swatch implementations coexisting in one file by design, which is a maintenance cost worth naming in the PR description, but it is not accidental duplication.

**Recommendation:** the stale `overrideStyling.md` "Known gaps" bullet should be corrected as part of this PR — it currently reads as if a colour-swatch component already ships, which is exactly the kind of thing that causes a future duplicate build.

---

## 2. FILE PLACEMENT — inconsistent with practice, but NOT a documented rule violation

**CERTAIN: `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/` is nowhere stated as a rule.** I grepped `.claude/rules/`, `AGENTS.md`, and `.docs/`. Every hit is a passing path example, never a directive:
- `overrideStyling.md:98, 201, 220, 249` — cites `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/…` and `ui-kits/organisms/<name>/<name>.css.ts` as *examples of the co-location pattern*.
- `testing.md:16, 81` — cites `ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` as a *reference test*.
- `.docs/memory/projectState.md:54` — describes what SFCC-55 *did*, past tense.

The only **documented** layout rule is `conventions.md` > File naming and folder structure: *"each component lives in its own folder under `overrides/app/components/`"*, with `overrides/app/components/productTile/` as the worked example — i.e. flat, no `ui-kits` layer. `new-component/SKILL.md` step 2 repeats it verbatim: `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.tsx`. **By the written rules, `components/product-view/colourSwatches/` is compliant and so is `ui-kits/molecules/`.**

What actually exists under `ui-kits/`:
```
atoms/     zimmButton zimmIcon zimmLogo zimmModal zimmNavItem zimmProductDescription
           zimmProductModelInfo zimmProductName zimmProductPrice zimmProductStyleCode zimmTextInput
molecules/ zimmContactIconRow zimmInputAction zimmProductContent zimmProductMeta
organisms/ zimmSubscribeModal zimmSubscribeSection
```

The nearest thing to a stated *purpose* is `CODEOWNERS:173-176`: *"ui-kits/ atoms, molecules, and organisms are **the shared design-system layer consumed by both squads' component overrides**"*. `ColourSwatches` is PDP-specific with a single consumer, so on that reading placing it outside `ui-kits/` is defensible — arguably correct. It's also the reading the auto-generated registry took: `.claude/registry/components.md` classifies it `Custom | 4 — Feature-local | Shared`, versus the ui-kits components which carry shared/protected tiers.

**Verdict: judgement call, no rule breached.** It is inconsistent with SFCC-89's `ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductMeta` and `zimmProductContent`, and that inconsistency is worth a deliberate decision rather than drift — but do not let a reviewer cite a rule here, because there isn't one. **Severity: nit** (consistency), and separately a **should-fix on the docs**: if `ui-kits/` placement is the intended default, `conventions.md` is the file that has to say so.

Also **CERTAIN and clean**: the `colourSwatches` camelCase folder inside the kebab-case `product-view/` override folder is exactly right per `conventions.md` — *"Zimmermann-authored files and folders: `camelCase`"* / *"Override files (mirroring a base Salesforce file): keep the original kebab-case filename"*.

---

## 3. NAMING (`Zimm*` prefix) — UNDOCUMENTED

**CERTAIN.** No `.claude/rules/*.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.docs/architecture.md`, `.claude/skills/new-component/SKILL.md`, or `.claude/registry/*.md` file states a `Zimm*` prefix convention. `components.md`'s only naming rules are *"Named export matches the folder name"* and *"Props type name matches the component name"* — both of which `ColourSwatches` satisfies (`colourSwatches/` → `export { ColourSwatches }`, `ColourSwatchesProps`).

It is purely observed practice, and the practice is not universal either — `BottomBar` (`overrides/app/components/footer/bottomBar/index.tsx`) and `FooterNavColumn` are Zimmermann-authored and unprefixed. The pattern that actually holds is: components inside `ui-kits/` are `Zimm*`-prefixed; components outside it are not. `ColourSwatches` sits outside `ui-kits/`, so it is consistent with that.

**Severity: nit / no action.** Do not raise this as a violation.

---

## 4. CSS / RECIPE STRUCTURE — structurally correct, two false "no token exists" claims

Compared `colourSwatches.css.ts` against `footer/footer.css.ts`, `footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts`, and `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`.

**CLEAN (all CERTAIN):**
- Namespacing: `export const ZimmColourSwatches` (line 3) — `Zimm*`-prefixed exactly like `ZimmFooter` / `ZimmFooterBottomBar`, so it cannot deep-merge into a base SFCC recipe. Satisfies `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.
- Registration: `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts:20` (import) and `:42` (in the `components` map) — the co-location pattern requires this and it's done.
- `var(--zimm-*)` usage: every colour/spacing value is a var reference, no bare Chakra token keys. I verified all 12 distinct vars used actually exist in `theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts` — none silently resolve to nothing.
- `textStyle: 'caption'` (lines 31, 37) stays a bare key — correct per `css.md`: *"`textStyle` stays a bare key — it's the one entry in the hierarchy that isn't a colour/spacing token."*
- Multipart `parts` array declared (lines 4-15), covered by `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` (which walks all of `overrides/app/components`, so this file is in scope despite sitting outside `ui-kits/`).
- No media queries at all — so the "explicit media queries, not Chakra array shorthand" rule is not engaged. Not a deviation; the component is a fixed-width 188px block. Worth confirming with design that's intended at mobile, but that's a design question, not a structural one.

**SHOULD-FIX — `audit-allow` suppresses two values that DO have tokens. CERTAIN.**

`overrides/app/components/product-view/colourSwatches/index.tsx:212-213` and `:222-223`:
```
{/* audit-allow: 16px icon size; no zimm token for swatch control dimensions */}
<ChevronLeftIcon boxSize="16px" />
```
`overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts:8-12` defines `iconSizes = { lg: '20px', md: '16px', sm: '12px' }`, and `zimmTokens.ts:189` exports `'--zimm-icon-size-md': iconSizes.md`. **A token for exactly this value exists and is named for exactly this use.** Should be `boxSize="var(--zimm-icon-size-md)"`.

`colourSwatches.css.ts:88, 94-95`:
```
// The three 2px sides have no foundation token; provisional: pending a dedicated --zimm-focus-ring-offset token.
inset: '-2px -2px calc(-1 * var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-secondary)) -2px',
```
`spacing.ts:33-36` defines `focusRingOffsets = { default: '2px', secondary: '3px' }` and `zimmTokens.ts:69` exports `'--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default'`. The comment says the dedicated token is pending; it already exists, and the file uses its sibling on the same line.

This matters beyond tidiness: `overrideStyling.md` states the `audit-allow` escape hatch is for *"a raw hex/px/rem/em literal … If this genuinely has no token yet"*. Using it where a token does exist trains the audit to be ignored. `24px`/`47px`/`72px`/`188px` genuinely have no token — those exceptions are legitimate.

Confirmed via `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`: all 12 of this PR's raw values land in the "acknowledged exception" bucket; the 4 unacknowledged violations it reports are all pre-existing (`header/index.tsx:238`, `theme/components/header.ts:73-74`, `navConstants.ts:5`) and untouched by this PR.

**NIT:** `colourSwatches.css.ts:61` `'&:disabled': { opacity: 0.3, … }` — a raw design value not covered by the file's `audit-allow` header list (which enumerates `188px, 47px, 72px, 24px, -2px`). The audit script only looks for px/rem/em/hex so it doesn't catch a bare float, but it's still an unnamed design decision.

---

## 5. OVERRIDE CORRECTNESS — CLEAN

**CERTAIN.** I enumerated every `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` import across all eight new/changed source files and cross-checked each against the actual override surface (`overrides/app/components/` contains only `_app-config, contentful, footer, foundation, header, icons, pageContainer, product-view, ui-kits, uiCopyProvider`).

No base-path import of a locally-overridden component anywhere:
- `colourSwatches/index.tsx:4` — `import { ChevronLeftIcon, ChevronRightIcon } from '../../icons'` — relative, correct. `icons` **is** overridden, so a base-path import here would have been the exact bug `overrideStyling.md` describes. Verified both icons are real exports: `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx:108, 114`, reaching `index.tsx` via `export * from './zimm'` (line 8), and `index.tsx:19-21` carries a comment explaining they're deliberately *not* re-exported from base. Also satisfies AGENTS.md's icons rule.
- `product-detail/index.tsx:64-66` — `ProductView` imported relative (`'../../components/product-view'`), correct.
- `staticProductHeader.tsx:3-5` — `shared/ui`, `breadcrumb`, `product-tile/promo-callout` all via base path; none has a local override, so base path is correct (and the file's own comment at lines 7-14 states this accurately).
- `product-view/index.tsx:61-77` — `image-gallery`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `link`, `product-tile/promo-callout` via base path; none is overridden. Consistent with overrideStyling.md's own note.

The `product-tile` `DisplayPrice` known-issue in the docs is not touched by this PR.

---

## 6. SFCC-89 INTEGRATION — clean extension, one placement question

**CERTAIN: `afterContent` does not bypass or duplicate anything `ZimmProductContent` offers.** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductContent/index.tsx:34-43` renders exactly three fixed children (`ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmProductDescription`) inside a `chakra.div` and accepts **no `children` prop and no slot of any kind**. Its JSDoc (lines 27-33) explicitly states model copy and style code are *"deliberately not here… the page positions them itself"* — so the established SFCC-89 pattern is already "the page composes around this molecule", and `afterContent` follows it rather than fighting it.

Adding `afterContent` to `StaticProductHeader` (types at `partials/staticProductHeader.tsx:19-22`, destructured at `:49`, rendered at `:104`) rather than widening `ZimmProductContent` is the right call: it keeps the molecule's fixed three-part contract intact, and it preserves the header's documented design goal (`:32-40`) of keeping its prop surface pinned to `ProductViewHeaderProps`.

**SHOULD-FIX — `{afterContent}` is rendered *inside* the loading Skeleton. CERTAIN about the code, SPECULATING about visual impact.**

`staticProductHeader.tsx:89-105`:
```tsx
<Skeleton isLoaded={Boolean(info)} minHeight="var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)">
  {info && ( <ZimmProductContent … /> )}
  {afterContent}
</Skeleton>
```
`afterContent` sits inside the `Skeleton` but outside the `{info && …}` guard. While `info` is falsy the swatches render *under Chakra's skeleton shimmer treatment*, and the `minHeight` on that Skeleton is sized for one line of product-name text, not for a 72px swatch row. Whether the swatches are visible-but-shimmering or clipped depends on Chakra's `Skeleton` implementation — I did not render it, hence SPECULATING on the visual. Structurally, the swatches are not part of the name/price group whose load state that Skeleton represents, so placing them as a sibling *after* the `</Skeleton>` (before the promo-callout Skeleton at `:107`) is the cleaner expression of intent.

---

### A. BLOCKER — the 11 new Playwright specs will not run on this PR. CERTAIN.

`e2e/features/pdp/` and `e2e/tests/zimm/pdp/` are **new directories** in this PR (`git diff develop...HEAD --name-status -- e2e/` shows both spec and feature as `A`, plus an `M` on `ProductPage.js`). That makes this "a new area's first spec", which `testing.md` covers explicitly:

> **Adding a new area's first spec:** give it its own allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` job, tag every `test()` in it with the matching `{tag: '@area'}`, and add it to this section.

Tagging is done correctly — `SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches.spec.js:24` has `const TAGS = { tag: ['@pdp', '@SFCC-91'] }` applied to all 11 tests, and the `.feature` carries `@SFCC-91 @pdp`. **The `qa.yml` allow-list group was not added** — `.github/workflows/qa.yml:108` defines only `e2e_homepage`.

`testing.md` claims the consequence is a harmless full-suite fallback. **That text is stale and the workflow contradicts it.** `qa.yml:154-171`:
```bash
SCOPE="homepage"
while IFS= read -r f; do

done <<< "$ALL"
```
with the step comment at `:121-133` confirming *"anything that can't be narrowed to one area now resolves to `skip` instead of `full` (changed 2026-08-25)… a develop PR that can't be scoped gets **no PR-time E2E run at all**"*. This PR's diff touches `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**` and `e2e/tests/zimm/pdp/**`, neither in the homepage allow-list → `e2e_scope=skip` → `e2e-localhost` does not run.

The only pre-merge E2E is `e2e-browserstack`, which *will* fire (`qa.yml:183-191` regexes `SFCC-91` out of the branch name and `--grep`s `@SFCC-91`) — so there is a path, assuming BrowserStack secrets are set. But the Chromium desktop+mobile localhost gate, which is what actually runs on every other PR, is silently skipped.

**Tension worth surfacing to the developer:** the fix is a `qa.yml` edit, and `.github/workflows/` is **Tier 1** (`frozenFiles.md` > CI/CD Pipeline). Per AGENTS.md Hard Rule #2 this needs the file named explicitly and either the verified-session exception or a `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` review. It is a four-line addition (`e2e_pdp:` with `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**`, `overrides/app/components/product-view/**`, `e2e/tests/zimm/pdp/**`, `e2e/features/pdp/**`, `e2e/support/pages/ProductPage.js`) plus a matching `SCOPE` branch, but it is not a change to make silently.

The two existing story-backed specs (`SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js`, `SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`) have the same two deviations, so this is consistent with practice and inconsistent with the doc — one or the other should move.

`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:838`, changed by this PR:
```diff
-  variant={id === 'color' ? 'circle' : 'square'}
+  variant="square"

Good component, genuinely well-tested — but it doesn't currently clear the bar on **verification** or **scope**.

**2. Initial colour may never reach the URL** *(needs live check)*. On a master-product PDP with no `?color=` and empty `variationValues`, the UI marks a swatch `aria-checked` while `variationParams` stays incomplete → Add to Bag shows *"Please select all your options above"*. Worse for a **single-colour** product: `hasOfferedColour` suppresses the base SwatchGroup, and `ColourSwatches` needs `length > 1` to render a radio — so there's no colour control anywhere.

content.content:
════════ overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:107 Two defects in this block. **1. The labels are English literals.** `config/sites.overlay.js:40-42` configures three non-English locales: ``` ZimmermannEUfr locales: [{ id: 'fr', alias: 'fr-eu' }] ZimmermannEUit locales: [{ id: 'it', alias: 'it-eu' }] ZimmermannEUes locales: [{ id: 'es', alias: 'es-eu' }] ``` with compiled `fr`/`it`/`es` bundles present in `overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/`. On `/fr-eu/`, every other PDP string renders in French and this one renders `Was 795,00 € Now 595,00 €`. The sibling atom in this folder handles it: `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:34-39` routes its label through `intl.formatMessage` with an inline `defaultMessage` in the base template's `product_view.label.*` namespace. Its docblock also records why `useUiCopy` is wrong for this — `useContentful.ts` requests entries with no `locale` parameter, so all eight storefronts get the space default. `defaultMessage` means no `translations/` change is needed. Suggest a placeholder rather than concatenation, so a locale can reorder: ```ts const WAS_PRICE_MESSAGE = { id: 'product_view.label.was_price', defaultMessage: 'Was {price}' }; const NOW_PRICE_MESSAGE = { id: 'product_view.label.now_price', defaultMessage: 'Now {price}' }; ``` Note the test cost: adding `useIntl` here fails all 8 tests in `index.test.tsx` with react-intl's `invariantIntlContext`, because they render with no provider. `zimmProductStyleCode/index.test.tsx:27-32` has the `renderWithIntl` wrapper to copy. Stories are unaffected — `.storybook/preview.tsx` supplies a provider. **2. No text node joins the two spans.** With `aria-atomic="true"` on the container, the whole string is read as one utterance. Actual assertion output: ``` expected 'Was $795.00Now $595.00' to be 'Was $795.00 Now $595.00' ``` The current tests can't detect this: they assert each span separately (`:47-48`, `:82-83`) and only check combined `textContent` on the non-sale variant (`:21`). `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:60-65` fixes the identical case with an explicit `{' '}`, noting that a whitespace-only flex item adds no width (CSS Flexbox §4), so the recipe's `gap` remains the only spacing. Verified both together: `tsc` clean, and one added assertion on the container's `textContent` takes the suite to 390/390. That assertion fails against the current code. ════════ overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:88 This branch measures 0px, so it does not reserve the layout slot it exists to reserve. The spans contain a single collapsible space. Blockified as flex items, that space is stripped, no line box is generated, and the flex `

` collapses. Measured in headless Chromium using the CSS the recipe actually resolves to: ``` as shipped (span = " ")

height = 0 spans = 0 / 0 settled price (reference)

# PR #70 review — draft for posting

Two parts: the general review body, then each inline thread with its anchor.
Nothing has been posted. Everything below was reproduced on `f9c6c74`; every suggested fix
was applied and verified before being written up, then reverted.

---
---

# PART 1 — General review body  (verdict: REQUEST CHANGES)

## Review — SFCC-91 colour swatches & variation selection

Requesting changes on one defect that makes a whole product class unpurchasable, one
out-of-scope change to a shared component, and a lint regression. Everything below was
reproduced by running it on this branch, and each suggested fix was applied and verified
before being suggested.

Gate results on `f9c6c74`:

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `npm run test` | 407/407 pass |
| `npm run audit:tokens` | no new violations — the 4 failures are pre-existing in `header/` |
| `npm run lint` | **30 problems, 9 of them new here** (develop baseline: 19) |
| CodeRabbit CLI (`--light --base develop`) | 1 critical, 1 major, 4 minor |

The component itself is good work — the roving-tabindex radiogroup, the DIS-scaled swatch
URLs, and the 19 unit tests plus 5 story `play`s are all solid. I broke the AC5 filter on
purpose to confirm the suite bites: it fails 3 tests. The problems are in the wiring around
it, not in `colourSwatches/`.

The blocking one, threaded on its own line:

- A single-colour product loses its only colour control, and Add to Bag is then permanently
  blocked behind "Please select all your options above". This is AC1's own scenario.

Then two that don't block but shouldn't merge as-is:

- `variant="square"` restyles colour swatches on five surfaces this ticket doesn't own.
- Two `audit-allow` comments claim no token exists where one does, in both cases named for
  exactly this use.

### Three items GitHub can't anchor

**`.github/workflows/qa.yml`** — `detect-changes` defines only an `e2e_homepage` allow-list,
so every path in this diff falls outside it and `Compute E2E scope` resolves
`e2e_scope: skip`. `Playwright E2E (localhost)` will report `skipping` rather than running.
The 11 new specs are tagged correctly (`['@pdp', '@SFCC-91']`) — the area group they need
was just never added. Combined with all 11 specs being `test.skip`-gated on unprovisioned
SKUs, and no unit test touching `handleColourSelect` / `history.replace` / `?color=`, **AC4
currently has no executing coverage at any layer.** BrowserStack will fire (the branch name
carries `SFCC-91`), but every spec it greps skips.

Fixing this means adding an `e2e_pdp` group, which is a `.github/workflows/` edit — Tier 1
per `frozenFiles.md`. Worth naming explicitly and routing rather than folding into this PR.
Same gap I flagged on #68; it's now bitten twice, so it probably wants its own ticket.

**`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:254-257`** — the "Known gaps" bullet reads as though a
`ProductDetailOptions` component already ships "colour/size swatches, quantity, and add to
bag". No such component exists under `overrides/` on this branch or on `develop` — it's an
unmerged f2r prototype, registered `placeholder: true`. I checked specifically because a
pre-existing colour-swatch implementation would have made this whole PR a duplicate. It
isn't one. But the bullet is exactly the kind of thing that causes a duplicate build later,
and this PR is the natural moment to correct it.

**PR body** — the changed-files table lists 15 of 27 files. The omissions include
`overrides/app/utils/filterImageGroups.ts`, `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` (+61 lines),
`e2e/support/pages/ProductPage.js`, and nine translation files. `translations/` and
`overrides/app/static/translations/` are **Tier 2** (`protectedFiles.md`), so this PR already
needs a tier-2 approver and the table doesn't say so. One of those files also picks up

Running your method properly killed two findings and promoted one.

**Promoted to blocking** — and it's not the one CodeRabbit found:

CodeRabbit's Critical said the initial colour never reaches the URL. It missed `params.get(key) || variationValues?.[key]` (`use-variation-params.js:46`), which rescues variant products. But chasing that fallback surfaced the real defect: **a single-colour product loses its only colour control.** `hasOfferedColour` is true at one colour → suppresses the base SwatchGroup; `ColourSwatches` needs `length > 1` → renders nothing clickable. Reproduced:

```
firstOfferedColour !== undefined  => true   (suppressColourAttribute={true})
queryAllByRole('radio')           => 0
queryAllByRole('button')          => 0
queryAllByRole('link')            => 0
getByText('Bay Blue')             => present
```

`validateOrderability` then returns false on `variationAttributes.length > 0 && !variant`, so it's *"Please select all your options above"* with nothing on the page that can satisfy it. Ironically that's AC1's own scenario. Fix applied and verified: `tsc` clean, 407/407.

**One CodeRabbit finding I'm rejecting outright** — its minor asking to revert the `Quantity:` change. `develop` had the same message id with two conflicting `defaultMessage`s (`:761` `'Quantity'`, `:857` `'Quantity:'`), and no locale stored the colon. **Two `audit-allow` comments were factually wrong**, both verified by applying the fix: `--zimm-icon-size-md` (16px) and `--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default` (2px) both exist and are named for exactly those uses. With both applied the component's acknowledged-exception list drops 10 → 5, and the 5 remaining are genuinely token-less.

## One thing I'd flag about my own evidence

I proved the single-colour chain in code and reproduced the missing-control half as a test, but I **did not drive a real master-product PDP in a browser** — the rendered outcome is inferred from the hook chain. I've said exactly that in the thread rather than overstating it. Worth one manual check before merge either way.

# PART 3 — Figma comparison (added after design check)

Checked against `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` (`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`), nodes
`40001992:51881` (Colour Options), `40000307:13823` (pdp/product-colour-picker),
`40000343:9726` / `40000307:14062` (pdp/product-content, Desktop Default) and
`40000343:9727` (Mobile Default).

Note: the ticket's own Design/Technical Notes point at a **different file** —
`QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (`Zimmermann_Final-Approved-Designs`, node `3087-15747`). Everything
below is measured against the Design System file that was supplied for review. Worth settling
which of the two is leading before acting on the geometry items.

The fourth URL, node `40003912:6219`, returns "node ID was not found in the file" — deleted,
or the ID is off. Nothing checked against it.

## What matches — no action

- **Colours are exact.** `alias/color/bg/surface/default` `#f6f4f1` → `--zimm-color-bg-02`
  (`ivory[200]` = `#f6f4f1`). `alias/color/field/border/focus` `#191919` →
  `--zimm-color-border-focus` (`grey[900]` = `#191919`). Both resolved through the foundation
  files, not eyeballed.
- **Typography is exact.** Figma's `Default/Caption-strong` is size 12px / weight 500 /
  line-height 18px / letter-spacing 0. `textStyle: 'caption'` resolves to `fontSizes['3xs']`
  0.75rem = 12px, `lineHeights['2xs']` 1.125rem = 18px, `letterSpacings.sm` = 0,
  `fontWeights.medium` = 500. All four line up.
- **The 44px / 28px spacing is right, and Figma-derived.** `40000307:13966` sets
  `gap-[var(--alias/space/1100,44px)]` between the content block and Colour Options, and
  `40000307:14062` sets `gap-[var(--alias/space/700,28px)]` to the size selector. The
  `marginTop: var(--zimm-scale-1100)` (44px) and `marginBottom: var(--zimm-scale-700)` (28px)
  match both.
- **Chevrons are exact** — Figma `40003328:115591` is a 24px hit area with a 16px icon, which
  is what the recipe and JSX do. The `Figma node 40000307-13867` reference in the code comment
  is the correct node.
- **Both pagination annotations are honoured** — "Pagination appears if there are more than 4
  swatches" matches `showPagination = swatchVariants.length > PAGE_SIZE`, and "If Label/Colour
  name is longer, use truncation" matches the ellipsis on `selectedName`.
- **No gap between swatches** — Figma's Swatches row is a plain `flex items-center` with no
  gap, same as `swatchGroup`.
- **`mix-blend-multiply`** is on the Product wrapper in Figma and on `swatchImage` here.
- **Not implementing "Small (Rounded)" / "Also available in"** (`40001992:51882`) is correct —
  that's the cross-product related-colours treatment, which is SFCC-708.

## What doesn't match

### 1. Swatch is 48px wide in Figma, 47px in code

`40000307:13826` / `:13831` / `40002689:3839` are all `h-[72px] w-[48px]`. Height matches;
width is 1px short. It propagates: the recipe's `width: '188px'` is commented
"PAGE_SIZE (4) × swatch width (47px)", and Figma's standalone `Type=Large (Squared)` frame is
**192** wide — 4 × 48.

### 2. The container shouldn't have a fixed width at all

In Figma the Colour Options block is `w-full` inside the product-content panel, and the
instance measures **338 × 104 on mobile** (`40000343:9727`) and sits in a 218px panel on
desktop. The 192px of swatches are left-aligned inside that full-width row; the label row
spans the whole panel.

`container: { width: '188px' }` pins the entire block — label row included — to 188px on every
breakpoint. The colour name therefore truncates ~30px earlier than designed on desktop and
~150px earlier on mobile, and the chevrons sit that far in from the right edge instead of at
it. Dropping the fixed width and letting the block be fluid is closer to the design than
correcting 188 → 192 would be.

### 3. Label row is 6px short whenever there are 4 or fewer colours

Figma's `labelContainer` is `h-[24px]`, unconditionally. The recipe sets no height, so the row
is driven by its tallest child:

```
Figma            : 24 label + 8 gap + 72 swatch = 104   (instance height, desktop and mobile)
code >4 colours  : 24 + 8 + 72 = 104   the 24px chevron button sets the height
code <=4 colours : 18 + 8 + 72 =  98   caption line-height 18px, nothing else in the row
```

So the block is correct only when pagination happens to be showing. With 4 or fewer colours —
the common case, and the state the reference product is in — it renders 6px short. A
`height: '24px'` (or `minHeight`) on `labelRow` fixes it.

### 4. Label row gap is 4px where Figma has two different gaps

Figma nests them: `labelContainer` has `gap-[var(--alias/space/200,8px)]` and the inner
`Label group` (`40003328:115970`) has `gap-[4px]`. So it's 4px between "Colour:" and the colour
name, and 8px between that group and the pagination.

The recipe flattens label / selectedName / paginationGroup into one row with a single
`gap: var(--zimm-scale-2xs)` (4px), so the gap before the chevrons is 4px instead of 8px.
Wrapping the first two in their own 4px-gap flex box and putting 8px on `labelRow` reproduces
the design exactly.

### 5. The swatch image fills the box; in Figma it floats in the ivory field

This is the most visible of the five. Figma's Product is `aspect-[1000/1300]` with
`flex-[1_0_0]` inside a 48 × 72 box that centres it:

```
Figma : w=48, h = 48 x 1.3   = 62.4  ->  9.6px of #f6f4f1 showing, split top and bottom
code  : w=47, h = 47 x 55/36 = 71.8  ->  0.2px  — effectively edge to edge
```

The `36 / 55` ratio in `swatchImage` isn't a design value; it's what you get from dividing the
(already 1px-short) 47 × 72 box. Figma's ratio is 10:13, and there's a designer annotation on
`40000307:13831` stating **"Image aspect ratio - 2:3"** for the box itself — which 48:72 is
exactly and 47:72 isn't.

Same error carries into the DIS request. `SWATCH_IMAGE_HEIGHT = 147` is `96 × 55/36`; at the
Figma ratio it should be `96 × 1.3 = 125`. The width and `q=60` are fine — only the height is
derived from the wrong ratio.

### 6. Focus ring right inset

Figma's Large/Rectangle focus ring is `inset-[-2px_-2.13px_-3px_-2px]`; the recipe uses `-2px`
on all three non-bottom sides. The `-2.13px` looks like a Figma artefact of the 48px box rather
than an intentional value, so I'd leave it — noting it only so nobody "finds" it later and
treats it as a real discrepancy. The bottom `-3px` matches.

## Suggested wording for the recipe's header comment

Line 1 currently reads "Swatch and control dimensions have no zimm foundation token — confirmed
by designer." The first half is true; the second half now reads as if the *values* were
confirmed, which the Figma file contradicts on width. Worth narrowing it to say the values come
from `40000307:13823` and that no foundation token exists for them yet.

I just tried to close the biggest gap and **couldn't.** Here's the honest audit.

## Solid — I ran it and read the output

`tsc` exit 0 · `npm run test` 407/407 · mutation check (AC5 break → 3 failures) · `npm run lint` 30 vs develop's 19 with all 9 new ones git-blamed · `audit:tokens` failures byte-identical on develop and in files not in the PR · both token fixes applied → tsc clean, 407/407, audit list shrank 10→5 · the URL-sync fix applied → tsc clean, 409/409 · the single-colour repro test · duplicate message id at `:761`/`:857` · en-US British spellings and `en-US` being a live locale · 3-of-11 locale coverage · `filterImageGroups` exported at `product-utils.js:182` and imported from that same module at `:26` with no test · `qa.yml`'s `SCOPE="skip"` shell · all 11 specs `test.skip`.

Those I'd defend as-is.

## Not verified — and one of them is under the blocker

**1. That master products lack top-level `variationValues`.** This is the load-bearing link in the blocking finding. The mock I cited is a **variant** (`type: {variant: true}`). I just went looking for a master fixture to confirm the negative — the only candidates are nested inside product-set/bundle fixtures and the extraction was inconclusive. **So that step rests on SFCC API knowledge, not observation.** If masters *do* carry `variationValues`, the single-colour case still breaks (no control to click) but Add to Bag would work, which downgrades it from blocker to bug.

**2. I never rendered a real PDP.** The whole chain is code-traced. AGENTS.md forbids me starting the dev server.

**3. The Figma deltas are arithmetic, not measured.** On #68 you measured in headless Chromium and quoted real numbers. I computed `47 × 55/36 = 71.8` from the CSS. Deterministic, but not the same standard.

**4. "~30px / ~150px earlier truncation" is soft** — it assumes the real PDP column equals Figma's 218/338 frame widths. The app's column is whatever the grid gives. The *direction* is right; those numbers shouldn't be quoted.

**5. Label row = 18px** — inferred from caption line-height, not measured.

**6. "Five surfaces" for `variant="square"`** — I confirmed 2 unsuppressed `<ProductView>` renders and 3 base importers, but I did **not** verify the `ccExtensibility` resolver actually redirects those base files. A subagent asserted it.

**7. `ProductDetailOptions` doesn't exist** — a subagent searched all refs. I didn't personally re-run it.

**8. The CodeRabbit CLI output** — a subagent ran it. I independently verified the Critical and rejected the Quantity minor; the other four I'm relaying.

## What I'd do before posting

Three are cheap and I can do them now:

- **#3 and #5** — render the component in headless Chromium via Playwright and measure the actual box heights, matching your #68 standard
- **#6** — read the `ccExtensibility` config and confirm the redirect

Until then I'd soften Thread 1 from "Add to Bag is blocked" to "no colour control renders; orderability likely blocked on masters — needs one manual check," which is still request-changes but doesn't overclaim.
